At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to restate this meaning, spoke in verse:
"In this present life, one experiences suffering and finds no joy; far removed from patience, one fosters hatred.
Enemies rejoice at every turn—such is the affliction of those who engage in conceptual proliferation."
The wicked Māra rejoices in this, and so do the members of Māra’s retinue;
all wholesome states are abandoned by those who engage in conceptual proliferation—such is their affliction.
Whatever wholesome deeds one intends to perform, through heedlessness one fails to abide in them;
through heedlessness one heads toward the evil realms—such is the affliction of those who indulge in frivolous proliferation.
Because they lack faith, their minds are difficult to subdue; Born into lowly families, they are constantly despised.
Their tongues are always stammering and faltering; Such are the afflictions of those who engage in frivolous discourse.
Because they preach the Dharma for others yet do not abide [in it], that Dharma does not manifest before them;
all spiritual friends abandon such persons, for those who engage in conceptual proliferation suffer from this affliction.
Constantly associating with all evil deeds, Extremely difficult to purify among the various vehicles,
Having no joy in hearing the words of the Dharma— Such are the afflictions of those who practice frivolous proliferation.
They encounter many obstacles to all that is wholesome; among all conditioned phenomena, they have many enemies.
When they exert effort, they meet with many hindrances; such are the afflictions of those who indulge in conceptual proliferation.
The wise understand these various afflictions; all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*) should be abandoned.
For those who practice proliferation, the Path is difficult to attain; therefore, one should not dwell in proliferation.
I shall flee by yojanas and further yojanas from all conceptual proliferation and contention;
I cannot dwell alone for even a moment in this place of affliction.
I have now left the household life seeking merit and virtue; do not engage in contention or give rise to evil thoughts.
Since there are no fields or goods for trade, for what purpose would you initiate strife?
Wife, sons, and servants, as well as houses and various possessions— having no such things,
and being free from the state of servitude, once you have gone forth, do not engage in strife.
Having already donned the robes of the kāṣāya, which are approved by the tranquil sages,
you who are endowed with these merits should abandon conceptual proliferation and give rise to patience.
The mind is like a venomous serpent and a rākṣasa; it will surely give rise to rebirth as hell-beings, ghosts, or animals.
For those who engage in frivolous conceptual proliferation, such a fate is not difficult to attain; therefore, one should apply diligent effort toward liberation.
All places of suffering, harm, and bondage—enmity, reproach, beating, and binding;
the gathering together and mutual contention—all that exists in the world abides herein.
If there is harmony, even enmity becomes difficult to overcome;
those who bring about harmony increase their renown, and those who bring about harmony attain mutual affection—how could a wise person fail to promote harmony?
Those who seek out faults find no opportunity; their kinfolk shall never be divided, nor shall their friends be scattered.
Having distanced themselves from conceptual proliferation, they will accord with the Teaching.
Within the Vehicle of Peace and Bliss, one shall attain purity; One shall be liberated from karmic obstacles without remainder.
Having subdued Māra and his hosts, One should give rise to patience when reviled by others.
If there is conceptual proliferation, there are many afflictions; for those without conceptual proliferation, their virtues are immeasurable.
I can manifest such things as these; if you wish to attain bodhi, you should give rise to patience.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is rare, World-Honored One!
Even to the point that the Tathāgata has spoken thus regarding the awakening of all afflictions.”
"Bhagavān! Will there be such bodhisattvas who, upon hearing this awakening regarding the afflictions in the future, will feel revulsion toward them?
And will they be able to sever them within the course of their afflictive conduct?"
The Buddha addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva, saying: “Maitreya!

In future ages, there will be few individuals (pudgala) who practice the vehicle of the bodhisattvas. During the final five hundred years, they will sever their afflictions; yet many will be stubborn and rigid, their minds lacking reverence, arrogant and self-exalting, making various conceptual discriminations and unable to engage in cultivation.”
Therefore, Māra Pāpīyān assumes the form of a bhikṣu and appears before them, creating such subversion as this:
"These sūtras are the compositions of others; they were not spoken by the Tathāgata."
Why is this? Because regarding the various merits described in this sūtra, there is neither "self" nor "other.

However, once that assembly has been defeated, they will harbor doubts and disputes concerning the various sūtras spoken by the Tathāgata; they will be unwilling to accept and uphold them, will not explain them to others, and will not practice them.
However, those deluded people do not understand it thus: "This is the retribution of various karmas; we shall be unable to realize such merit.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

The Tathāgata praised the ten kinds of arousal of the mind of Amitābha Tathāgata; if one arouses them by recollecting each accordingly—specifically, if one recollects with the desire to be born there—one shall immediately attain birth there.
“World-Honored One!
What are these ten kinds of resolve that arise in those places?
The Buddha addressed Maitreya, saying:
"The resolve they have made is not that of those with little wisdom; this resolve they have made is a matter of great significance.

All who wish to be born within the realm of Amitābha should give rise to a heart of loving-kindness and compassion for all sentient beings and refrain from harboring anger or resentment; thus shall they be born in the Buddha-realm of the Tathāgata Amitābha."
One should be born in that place for the sake of giving rise to compassion for all sentient beings;
because one has abandoned killing and upholds the True Dharma, having given rise to this mind, one shall be born in that place.
One should resolve to give up one’s body and life, for by not clinging to any phenomena, one shall be born in that place.
One should generate profound patience and practice pure faith; because one generates this mind, one shall be born in that place.
One shall be born in that place because one has generated this mind, which is unstained by fame, profit, or gain, and is a jewel of omniscience.
One shall be born in that place because one has generated a mind that gives rise to noble respect from all sentient beings and does not forget or lose it.
Because one gives rise to this mind that is neither startled, nor terrified, nor attached to ordinary speech, one shall be born in that place.
Because one gives rise to this mind that enters into the various roots of goodness of the factors of enlightenment, one shall be born in that place.
Nevertheless, because one gives rise to this mind without departing from the mindfulness of the Buddha, one shall be born in that place;
for it is free from all marks, Maitreya!

If a bodhisattva should give rise to each of these ten kinds of resolve and fully cultivate them, they shall be reborn in that land of Amitābha Buddha; it is impossible that they would not be so reborn.
At that time, the Elder Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is marvelous, World-Honored One!
It is even more so that the Tathāgata has preached this Dharma-text for the sake of awakening all bodhisattvas.”
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Elder Ānanda, saying: “Excellent, excellent, Ānanda!”
"Therefore, Bodhisattvas should awaken to this fundamental Dharma and uphold it in this manner.
When the Buddha had spoken this sutra, Maitreya Bodhisattva and the Elder Ānanda were filled with joy and leaped for gladness.

Those sixty sons of good family who practice the vehicle of the bodhisattvas all completely extinguished their karmic obstructions; with joy they received and practiced [the teaching], paid homage, and departed.
*The Sūtra on Arousing the Pure Mind*, Scroll Lower.
